cases.user_text: I had knee pain before insurance but it was never formally diagnosed. Does that automatically make it a pre-existing disease?

must_include: Explain that a symptom existing before insurance does not automatically settle PED status; the governed definition and relevant diagnosis/advice/treatment history matter.
legitimate_dependency: Whether this knee issue meets the applicable PED definition requires dates, medical history and the governing policy/regulatory context.
must_not_imply: Do not classify the knee issue definitively as PED or non-PED from this sentence alone.
acceptable_clarification: Ask about diagnosis, medical advice/treatment and dates if a personal determination is requested.
unnecessary_deferral: Give the general distinction before requesting documents.

cases.user_text: A doctor had only advised physiotherapy before I bought it. Does that change the answer?

must_include: Use the prior knee context and explain that prior medical advice or treatment can be relevant to the governed PED definition, so physiotherapy advice may matter.
legitimate_dependency: The exact effect depends on the applicable definition, timing and medical records.
must_not_imply: Do not conclude definitively that the knee condition is PED without checking the applicable criteria.
acceptable_clarification: Ask when the advice occurred and what the records show if a personal determination is requested.
unnecessary_deferral: Do not restart with a generic PED definition and ignore the physiotherapy fact.

cases.user_text: If I switch insurers next year, do I necessarily start the whole waiting period again?

must_include: Explain that switching insurers does not automatically mean all waiting-period credit is lost; continuity/portability rules can matter in the established PED context.
legitimate_dependency: Actual continuity or portability credit depends on applicable regulatory/product rules and continuous coverage history.
must_not_imply: Do not guarantee that all prior credit transfers or that the full wait always restarts.
acceptable_clarification: Ask for prior coverage dates and the new product only if an exact portability outcome is requested.
unnecessary_deferral: A general explanation of continuity/portability can be given without documents.
